key_insight: Cubic Discrete Diffusion enables tractable discrete generative modeling directly on high-dimensional pretrained representation tokens (e.g., 768–1024 dims) by factorizing the discrete distribution into a cubic structure, allowing rich semantic generation without collapsing to low-dim latents.
problem_solved: Existing discrete-token generation methods only work on low-dimensional latents (8–32 dims), losing semantic richness; this paper solves how to perform discrete diffusion and token prediction efficiently and accurately on high-dimensional representation tokens.
method: Define a discrete diffusion process tailored to high-dimensional representation tokens and noise schedules that preserve semantic structure during corruption and recovery.
Introduce a cubic factorization of the joint discrete distribution (3-way factorization) to make sampling, likelihood estimation, and learning tractable at large token dimensionality.
Integrate with pretrained high-dimensional visual representations so the model generates semantically rich tokens while keeping computational and memory costs manageable.
impact: Enables token-level generative modeling that preserves semantic detail from pretrained high-dim representations, bridging the gap between language-style token prediction and rich visual generation—useful for multimodal models, representation-based generation, and downstream fine-tuning.
visual_elements: Diagram of cubic factorization: high-dim token tensor split into three interacting factor matrices (illustrate reduction in complexity).

paper_title: Cubic Discrete Diffusion: Discrete Visual Generation on High-Dimensional Representation Tokens
paper_authors: Yuqing Wang, Chuofan Ma, Zhijie Lin, Yao Teng, Lijun Yu
